question: Researchers of which university produced India’s first gene-edited sheep?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sher-e-Kashmir University**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST), Jammu, is credited with producing India's first gene-edited sheep.
 
• This breakthrough was achieved using CRISPR-Cas9 technology, a revolutionary gene-editing tool.
 
• The gene-editing aimed to enhance specific traits, such as growth rate and wool quality, in sheep.
 
• The project was carried out under the supervision of experienced scientists specializing in genetic engineering and livestock improvement.
 
• This achievement positions India among the few countries utilizing gene-editing technology in livestock research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CRISPR-Cas9 Technology:**

 
 
• CRISPR-Cas9 is a precise gene-editing tool that allows scientists to modify DNA at specific locations.
 
• It works by using RNA molecules to guide the Cas9 enzyme to the target DNA sequence for cutting.
 
• This technology has applications in medicine, agriculture, and animal husbandry.
 
 
 
• **Gene Editing in Livestock:**
 
 
• Gene editing is used to improve livestock traits, such as disease resistance, growth rates, and reproduction efficiency.
 
• It is considered a sustainable approach to meet the growing demand for meat, milk, and wool.
 
 
 
• **Ethical and Regulatory Considerations:**
 
 
• Gene editing in animals is subject to ethical debates and regulatory approvals in many countries.
 
• India is exploring guidelines to ensure responsible use of gene-editing technology in agriculture and livestock.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Gene Editing in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Gene editing can enhance crop resilience to pests, diseases, and environmental stress.
 
• It plays a key role in ensuring food security and sustainability.
